silo_relevance: This paper is relevant to simulation_monte_carlo because it directly benchmarks its function-extraction approach against Monte Carlo integration values and frames the goal as producing a classically evaluable surrogate for a high-dimensional pricing function (C-001, C-011, C-040). For this silo, the main value is the reported compression/accuracy tradeoff relative to Monte Carlo-style estimates, rather than the broader tensor-network or quantum-circuit machinery (C-042, C-044).

key_points.point: The method is explicitly evaluated against Monte Carlo integration values for the worst-of put option, making Monte Carlo the direct baseline in the numerical test.
key_points.silo_note: This is the most direct simulation_monte_carlo connection: the paper compares its approximation to Monte Carlo outputs rather than only to an abstract exact solution.

key_points.point: The reported accuracy is within about 0.5 or less relative to Monte Carlo values, indicating the approximation can track simulation-based estimates closely.
key_points.silo_note: For simulation_monte_carlo, this suggests the reduced model may serve as a surrogate for repeated Monte Carlo evaluation in pricing workflows.

key_points.point: The MPS representation compresses the approximation from 1,048,576 cosine coefficients to 12,544 degrees of freedom while preserving near-overlap with the full cosine expansion.
key_points.silo_note: This matters for Monte Carlo settings because it points to a compact surrogate that could reduce the cost of repeatedly evaluating a simulation-derived pricing function.

key_points.point: The paper reports efficient classical evaluation cost O(dr^2D + rD^2) for the resulting approximation.
key_points.silo_note: In simulation_monte_carlo, a classically cheap surrogate is important when the goal is to replace or post-process expensive Monte Carlo estimates.

key_points.point: The authors frame the overall objective as obtaining an approximation efficiently computable on a classical computer, and note that direct amplitude readout is inefficient due to exponential suppression.
key_points.silo_note: For Monte Carlo applications, this highlights that the paper is not just about quantum state preparation; it is about extracting a usable pricing function that can compete with simulation-based methods.
